title: Thicker dirt, and the cement bottom becomes the bar
question: Is this the bed you asked for -- enough dirt, and no cement left over? Or should the dirt go deeper still and take height off the room?
context_md:
Your note today: *"we need a thicker layer of dirt, we don't need the giant cement bottom (although a lot of that should become the interface)."*

Same binary, same box, one number different: rows of soil under the surface. Everything above the ground line is untouched.

**Where the cement went.** The bed's floor now stops exactly where the button bar starts, so the stone left over is the eight-row lip you can see and everything below it is behind the bar.

**What it cost the crop: nothing measurable.** The worry was that a deeper bed starves the plants, and one earlier run said it did (725 plant cells down to 578). Over 12 worlds run side by side it does not reproduce -- the deep bed is ahead in 7 of 12 and behind in 5, and the light on the bench is identical to three decimals at every depth. What *does* use the extra depth is the ants: their tunnels were already reaching 35 rows into a 40-row bed, five rows off the stone.

It costs about a fifth more time per tick, paired and alternating, 5 runs of 5.

Shown paused at the start, before anything has grown, so the ground is the whole picture.

items.label: A -- before
items.caption: 40 rows of dirt on 64 visible rows of stone

items.label: B -- after
items.caption: 96 rows of dirt, an 8-row stone lip, the rest behind the bar
